threats.rationale: Use After Free needs manual deallocation. CLR objects are reclaimed by the tracing GC only when unreachable, so a live reference never dangles; the residual routes are NativePtr, P/Invoke, Marshal and Unsafe, which the library does not use (LogicGates.fs opens only System, line 3).

threats.rationale: The CLR turns a null dereference into NullReferenceException, not corruption, so the question is the WRONG error. `int` can never be null; the three N-ary gates take `int list`, a reference type. threats.name: Concurrent Execution Race Condition
threats.rationale: The gates have no fields and no module-level state, and every call has its own stack, so there is no shared state of their own. threats.name: Wrong operator or polymorphic comparison in a gate
threats.rationale: A gate is only operators. F# `=` is comparison (assignment is `<-`), `<>` is inequality, `&&`/`||` short-circuit while `&&&`/`|||`/`^^^` are bitwise; `&&&` on ints other than 0/1 gives other values. Structural `=` on an int is specialised and exact, so no polymorphic-comparison surprise exists for int, but would for a float (`nan <> nan`). A mis-typed operator in a gate flips a truth-table row; the 4-row domain {0,1}^2 is completely enumerated for every gate.
